# Cheatsheet {#sec-cheatsheet}

A one-page reference for the patterns this book uses, with the chapter that explains each.

## Front matter (YAML) {.unnumbered}

One source, several formats (@sec-compute):

```yaml
---
title: "Project Report"
author: "Author Name"
date: today
lang: en
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    format-links:
      - docx
      - {format: typst, text: PDF}
  docx: default
  typst:
    papersize: a4
---
```

More formats go in the same list:

```yaml
format:
  # html, docx and typst as above, then:
  pptx: default
  revealjs:
    output-file: report-slides.html
  epub:
    toc: true
```

## Code cells and inline code {.unnumbered}

Options go at the top of a cell, as `#|` comments (@sec-cell-options):

- `#| label: fig-name` numbers the figure and lets the text refer to it as `@fig-name`.
- `#| echo: false` hides the code and shows the output.
- `#| eval: false` shows the code without running it.
- `#| fig-cap: "…"` is the caption under a figure.
- `#| fig-alt: "…"` is the alt text screen readers announce.
- `#| tbl-cap: "…"` is the caption of a table.
- `#| output: asis` treats printed text as Markdown.

Inline code puts a computed value in a sentence (@sec-code-cells):

```markdown
The dataset contains `{{python}} len(df)` rows across `{{python}} df['year'].nunique()` years.
```

## Dashboards {.unnumbered}

A level-1 heading starts a page, a level-2 heading a row, and each cell's output becomes a card
(@sec-content-once):

````markdown
---
title: "Operations dashboard"
format: dashboard
---

# Overview

## Row {height=30%}

::: {.valuebox icon="trophy" color="primary"}
Most visited
`{{python}} top_name`
:::
````

The next row holds a chart:

````markdown
## Row

```{{python}}
#| title: Visits by attraction
fig = px.bar(attractions, x="visits_2025", y="attraction")
fig
```
````

Assign Plotly figures and end the cell with `fig`; never call `fig.show()` in a dashboard.

## Websites {.unnumbered}

`_quarto.yml` turns a folder into a website (@sec-london-website, @sec-water-website):

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  execute-dir: project
  pre-render: scripts/analysis.py
  render:
    - index.qmd
    - report.qmd
website:
  title: "My project"
  navbar:
    left:
      - {text: Report, href: report.qmd}
execute:
  freeze: false
```

A `menu:` under a navbar item makes a drop-down (@sec-london-website).

## Commands {.unnumbered}

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `uv init --bare` | starts a uv project in this folder |
| `uv add pandas matplotlib` | adds packages to `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, and installs them |

: The uv commands used in this book. {#tbl-cheat-uv}

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `uv run quarto preview file.qmd` | renders and serves a page, re-rendering on every save |
| `uv run quarto render file.qmd` | renders one file in all its formats (`--to docx`: one) |
| `uv run quarto render` | renders the whole project |
| `uv run quarto publish gh-pages` | the first publish to GitHub Pages, interactive |
| `uv run quarto publish gh-pages --no-prompt` | later updates, once the branch exists |
| `uv run quarto check jupyter` | shows which Python and Jupyter Quarto will use |

: The Quarto commands used in this book. {#tbl-cheat-commands}

## Check and undo with Git {.unnumbered}

Run them in the project folder, before and after every change, yours or the agent's
(@sec-first-git, @sec-first-change, @sec-git):

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `git init -b main` | starts a history here, on a branch called `main` (once per project) |
| `git status` | lists the files changed, added or untracked since the last commit |
| `git diff` | shows the changes not yet added, line by line (`-` old, `+` new) |
| `git log --oneline` | lists the commits, newest first, one line each |

: Looking at a project's history with Git. {#tbl-cheat-git}

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `git add .` | adds every change to the next commit (`git add report.qmd`: one file) |
| `git commit -m "What changed"` | records the added changes, with a message saying what changed |
| `git restore data/visits.csv` | throws away one file's changes since its last commit |

: Recording and undoing with Git. {#tbl-cheat-git-undo}

## Agent commands {.unnumbered}

Typed into the agent, not the terminal: @tbl-slash has the three that control cost and context.
OpenCode's names differ. `/models` picks the model, `/new` starts a fresh session in place of
`/clear`, and, as it has no `/exit`, Ctrl+C on an empty prompt quits (OpenCode
[TUI](https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/) and [keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds/)
documentation, checked 2026-11-20).

## Prompts {.unnumbered}

A reliable prompt (@sec-prompting):

1. **Names the inputs and outputs**: file names and column names, in backticks.
2. **Does one task.**
3. **Ends with a check**: "render it and tell me which file it wrote", "check the PDF is one page".
4. **Respects the data**: "compute every number from the cited files; never invent one".
